name: AC/DC: The "Back in Black" Beat
desc: AC/DC, Back in Black (1980)

name: The Bo Diddley Beat
desc: Bo Diddley, Bo Diddley (1958)

name: Queen: The "We Will Rock You" Beat
desc: Queen, News of the World (1977)

name: Four-on-the-floor rock
desc: Kick on every beat under a backbeat. Drives dance-rock and arena choruses.

name: Rock with sixteenth-note kicks
desc: Straight-eighth hi-hat with a kick figure on 3, the & of 3 and the a of 3.

name: Ride bell rock
desc: Ride bell on the beat, ride bow on the &. A bigger, brighter chorus sound than the hi-hat.

name: Floor-tom groove
desc: The right hand moves from the hi-hat to the floor tom for a darker, tribal verse groove.

name: Rock shuffle
desc: Triplet shuffle on the hi-hat (1 and let), backbeat on 2 and 4.

name: Double-kick sixteenths
desc: Constant sixteenth notes on two bass drum pedals under a backbeat.

name: Gallop
desc: Eighth and two sixteenths on the kick: the galloping rhythm of classic heavy metal.

name: Traditional blast beat
desc: Kick and cymbal together, snare in between, as fast as you can keep it even.

name: The Ronettes: The "Be My Baby" Beat
desc: The Ronettes, Presenting the Fabulous Ronettes Featuring Veronica (1964)

name: Michael Jackson: The "Billie Jean" Beat
desc: Michael Jackson, Thriller (1982)

name: Bee Gees: The "Stayin' Alive" Disco Beat
desc: Bee Gees, Saturday Night Fever soundtrack (1977)

name: The Motown Beat
desc: The Supremes, The Supremes A' Go-Go (1966)

name: Syncopated funk
desc: Hi-hat eighths, backbeat on 2 and 4, soft ghost notes between, kick on 1, the & of 2 and the & of 3.

name: Sixteenth-note ghost-note groove
desc: Hi-hat sixteenths with ghost notes on the e and a. Keep the ghosts barely audible.

name: Linear funk
desc: No two limbs play at the same time: kick, snare and hi-hat each fill their own sixteenths.

name: Paradiddle groove
desc: Paradiddle sticking (RLRR LRLL): right hand on the hi-hat, left hand on the snare with ghost notes and backbeats.

name: Half-time shuffle
desc: A triplet-based half-time shuffle: hi-hat on the 1 and let, ghosts on the trip, backbeat on 3. Made famous by Bernard Purdie.

name: Trap half-time
desc: Half-time backbeat on 3 under sixteenth-note hi-hats. Felt at 140 BPM.

name: R&B sixteenth groove
desc: A laid-back R&B groove with the kick pushing the & of 2.

name: Drum and bass two-step
desc: Kick on 1 and the & of 3, snare on 2 and 4. Felt at double time, around 174 BPM.

name: House
desc: Kick on every beat, open hi-hat on every &, clap or snare on 2 and 4.

name: The Bossa Nova Beat
desc: Stan Getz and João Gilberto, Getz/Gilberto (1964)

name: The Reggae One Drop
desc: Bob Marley and the Wailers, Survival (1979)

name: Dembow (reggaeton)
desc: Four-on-the-floor kick with the snare on the a of 1, the & of 2, the a of 3 and the & of 4.

name: Samba (kit adaptation)
desc: The surdo pattern on the kick (1, a, 2) with sixteenths in the hands. Felt in two.

name: Afro-Cuban 6/8 bell
desc: The standard 6/8 bell pattern over a dotted-quarter pulse on the kick.

name: Son clave (3-2) on cross-stick
desc: The 3-2 son clave on the cross-stick, with the bass-drum tumbao on the & of 2 and on 4.

name: Reggae steppers
desc: Kick on every beat, cross-stick on 3. A driving variation of the one drop.

name: Reggae rockers
desc: Kick on 1 and 3 with the cross-stick on 3. Busier than the one drop.

name: The Train Beat
desc: Johnny Cash, At Folsom Prison (1968)

name: 12/8 slow blues
desc: Four beats of triplets on the hi-hat, backbeat on 2 and 4. The feel of a slow blues.

name: Country boom-chick
desc: Kick on 1 and 3, cross-stick on 2 and 4: the classic country two-beat.

name: Gospel shout
desc: Fast eighth-note gospel feel with ghost notes filling every & on the snare.

name: The Swing Feel: Backbeat
desc: Snare on 2 and 4 with the hi-hat foot. Feather the kick.

name: The Swing Feel: Comp a of 2
desc: One snare comp on the a of 2. Hi-hat foot on 2 and 4.

name: The Swing Feel: Comp 3 & 4
desc: Snare comps on the a of 3 and the a of 4.

name: The Swing Feel: Bomb
desc: Comp on the a of 2, then drop a kick bomb on the a of 4.

name: Jazz Independence: Step 1
desc: Left hand: one snare note on the & of 1, between the ride notes.

name: Jazz Independence: Step 2
desc: Snare on 2 (with the ride) and on the & of 3 (between the ride notes).

name: Jazz Independence: Step 3
desc: Now the foot comps: kick on the & of 2 and the & of 4.

name: Jazz Independence: Step 4
desc: Snare on the & of 1, kick on the & of 3. Hands and feet in conversation.

name: Bebop: Time
desc: Ride, hi-hat foot on 2 and 4, feathered kick. Nothing else. This is the time everything sits on.

name: Bebop: Comp
desc: Left hand comps on the a of 2 and the a of 4, under the ride’s skip notes.

name: Bebop: Bomb
desc: Snare on the a of 1, then a kick bomb on the a of 3.

name: Bebop: Phrase
desc: Snare on the a of 1, 2 and 3, then the kick on the a of 4 sets up the next bar.

name: Jazz waltz
desc: Swing in 3/4: ride on 1, 2, the & of 2 and 3, hi-hat foot on 2 and 3.

name: Two-feel
desc: Ride pattern with a feathered kick on 1 and 3 and the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4, under a bass playing half notes.

name: Straight-Eighth Rock: Basic
desc: Kick on 1 and 3. Snare on 2 and 4.

name: Straight-Eighth Rock: & of 3
desc: Kick on 1, 3 and the & of 3. Snare on 2 and 4.

name: Straight-Eighth Rock: & of 2
desc: Kick on 1, the & of 2, and 3. Snare on 2 and 4.

name: Straight-Eighth Rock: Busy
desc: Kick on 1 &, 3 &. Snare on 2, 4 and the & of 4.

name: The 3/4 Feel: Basic
desc: Kick on 1. Snare on 2 and 3.

name: The 3/4 Feel: Pickup
desc: Kick on 1 and the & of 3, leading into the next bar.

name: The 3/4 Feel: & of 2
desc: Kick on 1 and the & of 2. Snare on 2 and 3.

name: The 3/4 Feel: Roll-in
desc: Kick on 1. Snare on 2, the & of 2, and 3.

name: The 16th-Note Feel: Basic
desc: Hats on every 16th. Kick on 1 and 3. Snare on 2 and 4.

name: The 16th-Note Feel: & of 3
desc: Kick on 1, 3 and the & of 3. Snare on 2 and 4.

name: The 16th-Note Feel: & of 2
desc: Kick on 1, the & of 2, and 3. Snare on 2 and 4.

name: The 16th-Note Feel: a of 4
desc: Add a snare on the a of 4 to push into the next bar.

name: Syncopated Reading: Line 1
desc: Snare on 1, 2, the & of 2, and 4.

name: Syncopated Reading: Line 2
desc: Snare on 1, the & of 2, 3, and the & of 4.

name: Syncopated Reading: Line 3
desc: Snare on the & of 1, 2, the & of 3, and 4.

name: Syncopated Reading: Line 4
desc: Snare on the & of 1, the & of 2, 3, and 4 &. Nearly all upbeats.

name: Open Hi-Hat: Step 1
desc: Open on the & of 4, close with the foot on 1.

name: Open Hi-Hat: Step 2
desc: Open on the & of 2 and the & of 4.

name: Open Hi-Hat: Step 3
desc: Disco: four on the floor, hat open on every &, closed on the numbers.

name: Open Hi-Hat: Step 4
desc: Kick on 1, the & of 2 and 3. Open on the & of 3.

name: Fills: Step 1
desc: Four 16ths on the snare on beat 4, then land on the crash.

name: Fills: Step 2
desc: Two on the snare, two on the rack tom, then crash.

name: Fills: Step 3
desc: Around the kit: rack tom, then floor tom, then crash.

name: Fills: Step 4
desc: Two-beat fill: snare on beat 3, toms on beat 4, then crash.
